facts.claim: Short-term dietary interventions are not typically successful in treating obesity and malnutrition.
facts.quote: however, the gut microbiome is generally resilient, and short-term dietary intervention is not typically successful in treating obesity and malnutrition.

facts.claim: Maternal intrapartum antibiotic exposure is linked to reduced diversity in the infant gut microbiome.
facts.quote: IAP, maternal overweight/obesity and excessive GWG were all associated with reduced diversity.

facts.claim: Diverse antibiotic regimens make it harder for the gut microbiota to control intestinal inflammation by altering the microbial community structure and microbiota-derived metabolites.
facts.quote: Diverse antibiotic regimens affect the ability of the gut microbiota to control intestinal inflammation in experimental colitis by altering the microbial community structure and microbiota-derived metabolites.

facts.claim: Antibiotics cause long-lasting detrimental effects on the host by compromising the composition and functions of the gut microbiota.
facts.quote: Antibiotics compromise the composition and functions of the gut microbiota inducing long-lasting detrimental effects on the host.

facts.claim: Increased exposure to antibiotics during early childhood is linked to reduced diversity of gut microbial species and the emergence of antibiotic-resistant microbes.
facts.quote: Increased exposure to antibiotics during early childhood increases the risk of antibiotic-associated dysbiosis, which is associated with reduced diversity of gut microbial species and abundance of certain taxa, disruption of host immunity, and the emergence of antibiotic-resistant microbes.

research.angle: While antibiotics are linked to reduced microbial diversity and long-lasting detrimental effects on gut function, the gut microbiome is generally resilient to short-term changes.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that antibiotics can cause long-lasting damage to gut diversity and function, particularly in early life, but the microbiome also demonstrates general resilience.
research.caveat: Many of the studies linking antibiotic exposure to reduced diversity are observational and lack longitudinal follow-up or standardized methodologies.
